sources.search_query: official France visa exemption list short stay site:service-public.gouv.fr OR site:diplomatie.gouv.fr
sources.relevant_excerpt: EES: A European database in which the Member States record the data of nationals of non-EU and non-Schengen Area countries who cross the external borders. [Gradual implementation began 12 October 2025; fully operational 10 April 2026. Applies to all third-country nationals entering for short stays (maximum 90 days per 180-day period), whether subject to visa requirements or not.] ETIAS: a travel authorization, distinct from a visa, comparable to the USA's ESTA or the UK's ETA; applies to nationals of the 59 visa-exempt countries entering the Schengen zone; fee EUR 20, waived for under-18s and over-70s; valid for multiple entries over 3 years, maximum stay 90 days per 180-day period. Expected to come on line in the last quarter of 2026. No websites currently issue ETIAS travel authorizations. BEWARE FRAUDULENT WEBSITES. Official resource: travel-europe.europa.eu
sources.effective_date_evidence: EES gradual rollout from 12 October 2025, fully operational 10 April 2026; ETIAS expected to come on line in the last quarter of 2026 (not in force as of 2026-07-23)

sources.search_query: us.diplomatie.gouv.fr US citizens visa waiver 90 days short stay France
sources.relevant_excerpt: Since April 1, 1949, France and the United States have had a bilateral agreement [allowing] U.S. citizens to spend 90 days in metropolitan France without requiring a visa, regardless of any previous stays in the Schengen zone. [This is] a 90-day stay under the Schengen visa exception covering U.S. citizens, in addition to 90 more days in metropolitan France. The bilateral agreement stay must take place after the Schengen visa exception stay. U.S. citizens must state their desire to invoke the bilateral agreement when they cross the border into France. A French border guard will then manually update their EES file so that the bilateral agreement is applied to their stay.
sources.effective_date_evidence: Bilateral agreement in force since 1 April 1949

policies.policy_name: Schengen short-stay visa waiver (59 visa-exempt nationalities)
policies.description: France applies the common Schengen short-stay visa policy. Per the MEAE, 59 nationalities are exempt from the short-stay visa for stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period ('Depending on your nationality and the type of your passport, you may be exempt from a visa'). The complete official list is served by the France-Visas 'Visa wizard', which was inaccessible to automated retrieval (HTTP 403); only USA membership was individually verified from an official French page. Visa-exempt travelers are subject to EES biometric registration at the external border and, from ETIAS go-live (expected Q4 2026), will need an ETIAS travel authorization.
conditions: Stay limited to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen Area
Complete nationality list not retrievable from reachable official pages; verify per nationality via the official France-Visas Visa wizard (france-visas.gouv.fr)

policies.description: European citizens can enter and be present for up to 3 months in France without special formalities, needing only a valid passport or identity document; no residence permit or work authorization is required. They are excluded from EES registration.
conditions: Applies to all EU, EEA and Swiss citizens (DEU and FRA listed here as the requested nationalities covered)
Valid passport or national identity card required for identity checks

The bilateral-agreement stay must take place after the Schengen visa-exception stay, and the traveler must state the desire to invoke the agreement at the French border so the EES file is manually updated. Tourism/short visits only.

policies.policy_name: Schengen short-stay (uniform) visa via France-Visas and local visa centre
policies.description: Non-exempt nationalities must obtain a Schengen short-stay visa before travel. The application is completed online on the official France-Visas portal, then submitted in person to the applicant's local visa centre or the French consulate in the country of residence; the portal also handles tracking. Applications may be lodged up to six months before departure. The visa allows up to 90 days (continuous or cumulative) in the Schengen Area per 180-day period.
conditions: Passport valid at least 3 months after the visa end date, issued within the last 10 years, at least 2 blank pages
Visa fee payable at lodging; amount published in the France-Visas 'Tarifs' section (not retrievable — see unresolved)
Statutory documents on purpose of stay, means of support and accommodation must be presentable at the border

policies.policy_name: ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) — not yet in force
policies.description: ETIAS is a travel authorization distinct from a visa, comparable to the USA's ESTA or the UK's ETA. It will apply to nationals of the 59 visa-exempt countries entering the Schengen zone. Fee EUR 20 (waived for under-18s, over-70s and certain family members); valid for multiple entries over 3 years; maximum stay 90 days per 180-day period. As of the retrieval date it is not operational: 'Expected to come on line in the last quarter of 2026' and 'No websites currently issue ETIAS travel authorizations.' Official EU resource: travel-europe.europa.eu.
conditions: Not in force as of 2026-07-23
Will apply only to visa-exempt (59-country list) short-stay travelers once live

policies.description: EES is a European database in which Member States record the data of nationals of non-EU and non-Schengen Area countries who cross the external borders. It applies to all third-country nationals entering for short stays (max 90 days per 180-day period), whether visa-required or visa-exempt, and replaces passport stamping. Biometric data collected: facial image and, for travelers 12+, fingerprints. Gradual implementation began 12 October 2025; fully operational since 10 April 2026. Registration is free. EU/Schengen citizens and nationals of Andorra, San Marino, Monaco and the Holy See are excluded.
conditions: Not a visa or authorization — a border registration system
Applies at the external borders of the 29 Schengen Area countries
